summary: The eligibility exception is guarded, but Team-first ordering still has four concrete bypasses when choosing an account.

findings.evidence: savedForUser is compared before afterTeams. With paceHoldsBackground enabled, an Opus failure can switch to an eligible, unsaved Ultra even when a usable Team has a free seat but is saved by its day's pace. decideSwitch passes this callback through to chooseAccount. The new ranking therefore leaves the pace-related part of R047-002 unresolved.
findings.fix: Compare afterTeams before savedForUser for Opus/Sonnet, preserving pace ordering within each account class. Cover this combination through failure switching and seat movement.

findings.evidence: The current-full branch excludes unknown accounts and never calls unreadTeamSeats or chooseTeamsFirst. Consider a project on an eligible Ultra with no free seats, another measured eligible Ultra with one free seat, and a logged-in unread Team with a free seat. server.ts supplies unreadTeams at line 5156, but this branch ignores it and moves the project to the second Ultra. This chooses a new account, so the accepted keep exception does not apply.
findings.fix: Include eligible unread Teams in seat-movement selection before considering exception Max/Ultra accounts, retaining known blocking windows and seat checks.

findings.evidence: The forAll pass filters accounts by freeSeats >= seatsWanted before Team priority is evaluated. A project asking for six seats on a full five-seat Team moves to an eligible Ultra with six free seats even when another usable Team has one free seat. server.ts:5173 supplies seatsWantedOnly for this crowded case, and its single-seat fallback runs only when the first decision is keep. Thus capacity preference overrides rule 2 during a new account choice.
findings.fix: For Opus/Sonnet, evaluate usable Teams with a seat before exception accounts, applying the preference for seats for the whole project within each class.

findings.evidence: Failure waits break equal reset times by current account and name, without Team priority. Suppose the failed Team resets in three hours, eligible a-ultra and usable z-team both have exhausted sessions resetting in one hour, and a-ultra's Fable and weekly reset together in 48 hours. Neither alternative runs now; the wait loop chooses a-ultra alphabetically and moves the project there. The Ultra does not free sooner than the Team, contrary to rules 2 and 5.
findings.fix: For equal availability times, prefer Teams over exception Max/Ultra accounts before applying current-account and name tie-breaks. Preserve the exception when the Ultra genuinely frees earlier.

coverage: Verified the plan hash, all 14 manifest file hashes, and the tracked diff hash; inspected every changed file's additions and relevant surrounding code.
Reviewed reserve eligibility, reset boundaries, absent and unknown windows, ranking, Haiku behavior, and related test assertions.
Traced placement, pins, failure and leftover retries, refresh rescue, switch-ahead, crowded seat moves, wait reconsideration, and final dispatch guards.
Inspected related usage parsing and caching, plan classification, pace state, project model and excursion state, seat admission, and esperandoTeam reporting.
limitations: Static inspection only; no files were edited, no tests or scripts were run, and no work was delegated.
Large existing files were inspected in relevant sections rather than exhaustively.
External operational measurements were unavailable for independent verification.
The accepted retention behavior from R047-001 was respected. The documented esperandoTeam mislabel from R047-004 remains.
